Start with the expanded examples. Open further examples for options and alternative R approaches.

rename

Rename a variable

Stata 

rename x x2

R dplyr 

rename(data, x2 = x)

Note the order: new name = old name.

Stata reference · R reference

4 more examples and alternatives

Rename several variables

Stata 

rename (a b) (c d)

R dplyr 

rename(data, c = a, d = b)

Stata reference · R reference

Add a suffix to every name

Stata 

rename * *_old

R dplyr 

rename_with(data, ~ paste0(.x, "_old"))

Stata reference · R reference

Make all names lower case

Stata 

rename *, lower

R dplyr 

rename_with(data, tolower)

Stata reference · R reference

Upper-case some names

Stata 

rename x*, upper

R dplyr 

rename_with(data, toupper, starts_with("x"))

Stata reference · R reference

replace

Change a variable

Stata 

replace x = x^2

R dplyr 

mutate(data, x = x^2)

Stata reference · R reference

2 more examples and alternatives

Change a variable under a condition

Stata 

replace x = x^2 if x > 0

R dplyr 

mutate(data, x = replace_when(x, x > 0 ~ x^2))

Differs from Stata Stata numeric missing values compare larger than every finite number; R comparisons return NA, and replace_when() leaves those rows unchanged. replace_when() needs dplyr 1.2.0 or later; with older dplyr, use if_else(x > 0, x^2, x).

Stata reference · R reference

Change a variable for some rows

Stata 

replace x = x^2 in 11/20

R dplyr 

mutate(data, x = if_else(row_number() %in% 11:20, x^2, x))

Stata reference · R reference

rnormal

Normal random numbers

Stata 

generate z = rnormal()

R stats 

mutate(data, z = rnorm(n()))

Differs from Stata R and Stata use different random-number streams; the same numeric seed does not reproduce the same draws or selected rows.

Stata reference · R reference

round

Round

Stata 

generate y = round(x, 0.1)

R base 

mutate(data, y = round(x, 1))

Differs from Stata R's second argument is the number of decimals. R rounds halves to even (round(0.5) is 0); Stata rounds them up.

Stata reference · R reference

runiform

Uniform random numbers

Stata 

generate u = runiform()

R stats 

mutate(data, u = runif(n()))

Differs from Stata R and Stata use different random-number streams; the same numeric seed does not reproduce the same draws or selected rows.

Stata reference · R reference

sum

Running sum

Stata 

generate cs = sum(x)

R dplyr 

mutate(data, cs = cumsum(coalesce(x, 0)))

Stata's sum() function treats missing values as 0, hence coalesce(x, 0).

Stata reference · R reference

tabulate

Dummy variables for every category

Stata 

tabulate x, generate(x_)

R tidystata 

as_dummy(data, x)

Differs from Stata as_dummy(data, x, .names = "index") numbers the columns x_1, x_2, ... as Stata does. Also: fastDummies::dummy_cols(data, "x"). as_dummy() defaults to value-based column names; .names = "index" gives numbered Stata-style suffixes. Check the missing-category indicator policy too.

Stata reference · R reference

tostring

Numbers to text

Stata 

tostring num_x, generate(str_x)

R tidystata 

mutate(data, str_x = tostring(num_x))

Differs from Stata Labelled values keep their codes; decode() gives the value labels instead. Formatting and retained precision can differ from Stata tostring; choose an explicit format when exact text or round-trip precision matters.

Stata reference · R reference

winsor2

Winsorise at the 1st and 99th percentiles

Stata 

winsor2 x, cuts(1 99)

R datawizard 

mutate(data, x_w = datawizard::winsorize(x, threshold = 0.01))

Differs from Stata datawizard uses R quantile cutpoints while winsor2 uses Stata percentile rules; small samples and ties can therefore yield different caps.

Stata reference · R reference

xtile

Quantile groups

Stata 

xtile q = x, nquantiles(4)

R tidystata 

mutate(data, q = xtile(x, 4))

xtile() follows Stata's rule, so equal values stay in the same group. Returns an ordered factor by default, or integer codes with labels = FALSE. Inside grouped mutate(), the default is integer codes; labels = TRUE explicitly requests labels.

Stata reference · R reference

1 more examples and alternatives

Weighted quantile groups

Stata 

xtile q = x [aweight = w], nquantiles(4)

R tidystata 

mutate(data, q = xtile(x, 4, wt = w))
